title: VM provisioning and ./lab VM lifecycle
objective: Make the VM reproducible and controllable from the host: ./lab can provision or connect to the VM per #40, install Docker, transport the workspace, and run VM lifecycle commands idempotently. The host stops running the agent container itself.

acceptance_criteria.text: One documented command/runbook takes a clean host to a working VM (Docker plus compose plugin, repo checkout, agent image) with a CPU-only path that works without a GPU.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Sixth 2026-10-28 non-clean CachyOS retry confirms enabled rootless user service still fails: RootlessKit reports no subuid ranges for mester; image build not reached. User-manager/linger/socket setup is valid. New subid helper validates/repairs exact mappings on each start and fails on overlap; KVM retry pending.

acceptance_criteria.text: ./lab gains VM lifecycle commands (names fixed by #40, for example vm up/status/ssh/down) that are idempotent: re-running does not duplicate VMs, disks or networks.

check_workspace() validation still runs on the host before a path is sent to the VM; /, $HOME, the lab repo without --unsafe-recurse, and sensitive credential directories are refused and never mounted.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Self-tests 1-6 pass: check_workspace rejects /, $HOME, sensitive dirs; accepts safe dirs; --unsafe-recurse allows repo

acceptance_criteria.text: The VM publishes no host ports by default; an automated check confirms the agent and workspace services are reachable only on the VM's internal Docker networks.

Model access follows #40: host-side ollama/llamacpp are reachable only through syntactically valid, narrow QEMU guestfwd ports; GPU passthrough is not required, and a CPU-only host starts with the same flow and a clear message.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: 2026-10-27: tests/vm.bats verifies narrow cmd:socat guestfwd targets for 11434/8080/3128; extracted QEMU 10.0.13 accepted the generated netdev argument and stayed alive until an intentional timeout. Live model connectivity on the CachyOS KVM host is still required.

acceptance_criteria.text: ./lab stop removes agent containers plus workspace containers, networks and volumes and VM-side state; git status --short in the real checkout is empty afterwards.
./verify-lab.sh passes from a clean clone inside the VM, and the run is recorded on this ticket.

The host no longer runs the agent container; any host-side Docker use is limited to a documented service (for example model servers) if #40 chooses that option. README and docs/01-host-setup.md describe the VM flow and remove dev-container-only instructions.

A10: Full lifecycle test on real KVM host passes end-to-end: base → up → status → ssh → agent test → stop → down. Procedure: 1) Verify host KVM: grep -c svm /proc/cpuinfo > 0; 2) Verify /dev/kvm accessible; 3) ./lab-vm base (downloads image, verifies hash); 4) ./lab-vm up (creates overlay, seed ISO, starts virtiofsd + QEMU); 5) ./lab-vm status (confirms PID, port); 6) ./lab-vm ssh (opens shell, verify /workspace virtiofs mount, docker info); 7) cd /workspace && ./lab --unsafe-recurse; 8) git status --short clean; 9) ./lab-vm stop (graceful shutdown); 10) ./lab-vm down (teardown)

A11: Prereq check auto-detects distro, maps packages correctly, prompts before installing. Procedure: 1) ./lab-vm base with missing deps — detect distro, list missing tools; 2) Display distro-mapped package names; 3) Verify [y/N] prompt, default N; 4) On Arch: verify virtiofsd symlink fallback for /usr/lib/qemu/qemu-virtiofsd; 5) After install, re-run: 'All VM dependencies found. OK'

A12: Idempotent lifecycle — re-running up/status/stop does not duplicate VMs or stale state. Procedure: 1) Run ./lab-vm up twice, no second VM; 2) Run ./lab-vm stop twice, second is no-op; 3) ps aux | grep qemu-system-x86_64 ≤ 1; 4) ps aux | grep virtiofsd ≤ 1
A13: Stale state cleanup — manually killed QEMU, ./lab-vm status detects stale PID, ./lab-vm down cleans sockets/PIDs, no orphaned processes, fresh base+up works

QEMU startup uses a valid end-to-end device configuration: guestfwd destinations use QEMU character-device syntax and host loopback targets, virtiofsd is paired with vhost-user-fs-pci plus shareable guest memory, the `workspace` tag is mounted at /workspace, and an immediate QEMU exit fails fast with the real exit status and qemu.log instead of waiting for the SSH timeout.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: 2026-10-28 owner CachyOS log at 7b54d26 proves QEMU KVM boot and SSH after corrected guestfwd/vhost-user-fs/shareable-memory argv. Provisioning then failed on nf_tables; generated mount code has regression coverage, but findmnt /workspace and full device/lifecycle proof remain pending.

acceptance_criteria.text: Clean pinned-Ubuntu provisioning loads guest nf_tables before unprivileged Docker setup and persists it across reboot; Docker proxy/non-overlapping CIDR config exists before first start. Diagnostics did not print current /etc/subuid,/etc/subgid, so underlying absence/reason unconfirmed. Current change adds exact mapping validation/repair and file/getsubids diagnostics before cleanup. Verify no overlap and rootless API on non-clean retry; persistence remains pending.

acceptance_criteria.evidence: 2026-10-28 fourth clean CachyOS run proves schema correction: cloud-init status done, extended_status done, errors=[], recoverable_errors={}, then readiness checks passed and agent image build began. Earlier diagnostic run identified groups.0.mester: [] defect and retained status2. No warning bypass used; original-status/diagnostic and generated-shape regressions pass. acceptance_criteria.text: SSH readiness uses a bounded single-Ed25519 scan without the tee|grep-q pipefail pipeline, records stderr/original failure status, and never writes known_hosts from a failed/partial/wrong-key scan. Record real guest boot/cloud-init versus SSH-ready elapsed times on clean and reused overlays; do not claim overall warm-start improvement from guest boot time alone.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: tests/vm.bats verifies bounded Ed25519-only successful scan, complete key write, partial/wrong-key rejection and stderr/status. Fourth clean host run reached SSH on attempt6 (~10s), versus prior reused-overlay run ~2m40 with old probe. Clean timing improved in this observation; warm restart after change still needed, so criterion remains in-progress.

acceptance_criteria.text: Non-interactive guest agent-image builds explicitly load client/auth-helper proxy environment, retain daemon proxy configuration and forward all six upper/lower-case build proxy arguments without baking proxy ENV into the image. Missing profile fails closed; build.log retains output and original pipeline status. Live Docker Hub base pull/auth, RUN package installation and completed agent image must succeed under restrict=on and the approved manifest.

evidence=".mester/logs/vm-host-$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S)"

BEFORE IMPLEMENTING A RELAY, DIAGNOSE THE PARTIAL PROXY FAILURE on the owner CachyOS KVM host; keep overlay, host-Docker session and credentials; do not use --clean/stop/down and do not build a relay yet. This workspace has no /dev/kvm or live guest. From host checkout terminal A run `./lab-vm up --debug --unsafe-recurse --auto-accept` without --clean. As soon as it prints `Building agent image inside VM...`, in terminal B run `./lab-vm ssh` and execute in the guest: `ip route; ss -ltnp; sudo -iu mester curl -sv --connect-timeout 4 -x http://10.0.2.100:3128 http://deb.debian.org/ -o /dev/null`; then check RootlessKit's actual `--cidr=10.0.3.0/24`, service Environment and daemon proxy settings. Confirm the cached `python:3.12-slim` image exists; inside a throwaway rootless container using that cached image, capture route data (`ip route` if installed, otherwise /proc/net/route) and test both TCP connect to 10.0.2.100:3128 and an HTTP request through that proxy to deb.debian.org. Record exact command/output/errno and guest/container routes plus `ss -ltn` where available. Do not retry build after the diagnostic run until these results are reviewed. This is intended to distinguish guestfwd reachability from nested route/CIDR collision; connection-refused alone does not prove the container landed on its gateway. Current `.mester-egress` already allows github.com, npmjs.org and deb.debian.org; security.debian.org is absent. Do not widen egress manifest without owner approval; if probes establish a policy-denial issue, request specific domain approval first.
Check .mester-egress domains against actual Dockerfile traffic (security.debian.org, deb.debian.org, github.com, npmjs.org). Ask owner before adding domains; do not modify allowlist without approval.

Agent build still failed at Dockerfile step 4/11 `npm install -g @opencode/cli` postinstall, so `opencode --version` and image export did not run. npm 9.2.0 / Node v20.19.2 fetched registry manifests (HTTP 200), downloaded the Linux x64, x64-baseline and musl tarballs (HTTP 200) and logged unpack complete; package postinstall nevertheless returned 1 with generic 'Failed to install OpenCode' and suggested platform packages. This rules against current proxy connectivity/registry-fetch failure but does not yet establish why postinstall cannot select the downloaded package. Startup cleanup stopped QEMU after failure; VM is not running. Preserve overlay; next action is targeted package/postinstall diagnosis, no --clean and no egress-policy changes.

2026-10-28 npm follow-up diagnostic implementation: because owner retry showed registry HTTP 200 and tarball unpack completion but only the postinstall's generic error, do not infer an egress or package-manager root cause. The next build changes install sequencing to expose optional-package presence/resolution and runtime platform details before executing postinstall; it does not change egress policy, VM state, or overlay. Targeted Bats/syntax checks pass; KVM retry remains pending. After this diagnostic revision is committed/shared, retry exactly `./lab-vm up --debug --unsafe-recurse --auto-accept` without `--clean`, stop after first failure, and return the platform diagnostics plus the postinstall/npm tail and exit status. If it succeeds, verify `opencode --version` and built image before claiming progress; full lifecycle remains outstanding.

2026-10-28 follow-up host build using diagnostic commit 6a70df7: cloud-init and rootless Docker passed; proxy reachability confirmed again (`proxy_tcp_errno=0`, HTTP 200). Script-free global npm install reports 5 packages added. The diagnostic found all four Linux x64 package.json files in the expected nested paths, but its `require.resolve(packageName)` check returned MODULE_NOT_FOUND for each. This does NOT prove packages are absent because the architecture packages may be binary-only and have no JS entrypoint; the earlier diagnostic therefore overinterpreted module resolution. Manual postinstall still returned the generic failure. Its handler displayed the latest npm log from `npm root -g`, not an install log, so that tail is irrelevant. VM is stopped after the failed build; overlay remains preserved. Corrected follow-up diagnostics now print candidate package metadata/file names and the CLI postinstall source; postinstall failures no longer claim a stale npm log. Do not repeat host build until corrected diagnostic revision is committed/shared. No egress change or clean retry.

2026-10-28 next CachyOS retry with postinstall source diagnostics: cloud-init/rootless/proxy all pass; BuildKit proxy probe succeeds TCP errno 0 / HTTP 200. All four Linux x64 optional package directories exist with `bin/opencode` and package.json, so neither egress nor missing downloads explain the failure. OpenCode's postinstall source shows it tries `require.resolve(<package>/package.json)`, copies the binary, then silently validates it by spawning `opencode --version` with stdio ignored; on any error it falls back to a temporary npm install and repeats. The generic final message therefore hides the cause (likely package resolution or binary execution); no specific cause is proven yet. QEMU was stopped by failure cleanup; overlay preserved. Follow-up local diagnostic now checks package.json resolution and executes each installed variant's `--version`, reporting spawn status/signal/error and output plus AVX2. No host rerun until this diagnostic patch is committed/shared; preserve policy and do not clean.

2026-10-28 CachyOS retry with commit dc5e896 provides the decisive cause: guest Node v20.19.2 reports Linux x64, glibc 2.41, `cpu_avx2=false`; OpenCode's baseline and regular Bun binaries both exit 134 with `this CPU is missing SSE4.2 support, which Bun requires. If this is a VM, enable host CPU passthrough (e.g. -cpu host for QEMU/KVM).` Both musl variants are not runnable due to ENOENT (expected for glibc host). Package resolution succeeds and all four tarballs/files exist. Root cause is QEMU's default KVM guest CPU model not exposing SSE4.2, not npm, registry or proxy. Targeted fix adds `-cpu host` for KVM (pass host features including SSE4.2) and Westmere for TCG (SSE4.2 without AVX2 to select baseline); adds argv tests. This preserves existing overlay, `restrict=on`, proxy, and allowlist. Local test/syntax validation pending; host verification must use existing overlay without --clean and only claim image success if opencode --version and build complete.
